title: Theseus and Athens
subtitle: Founders, civic myth, and contested versions

assessment.title: Theseus and Athens assessment
assessment.prompt: Five new questions revisit the week’s events, interpretations, and source distinctions. Taking the assessment completes the week; missed answers remain practice priorities.

question.prompt: Which source supplies this biographical framing?
question.explanation: Plutarch’s Life of Theseus is the passage-specific answer. Check Plutarch: Lives of the Noble Grecians and Romans (Life of Theseus, road to Athens), keeping each work and version distinct.

question.prompt: What does Ariadne's clue let Theseus do in the Epitome?

choices.text: Find his way out after killing the Minotaur.

question.explanation: The Epitome says Theseus draws the clue after him as he leaves the labyrinth.

question.prompt: What changes when the hero becomes a civic founder?

choices.text: His story ceases to have political meaning.
The source becomes an eyewitness record of prehistoric Athens.
His deeds explain the community’s institutions and belonging.

question.explanation: His deeds explain the community’s institutions and belonging. is the passage-specific answer. Check Plutarch: Lives of the Noble Grecians and Romans (Life of Theseus, unification of Attica), keeping each work and version distinct.

choices.text: Plutarch reports alternatives; his report does not establish one eyewitness history.
All variants must have happened consecutively.
A later biography cannot preserve any earlier traditions.

question.explanation: Plutarch reports alternatives; his report does not establish one eyewitness history. is the passage-specific answer. Check Plutarch: Lives of the Noble Grecians and Romans (Life of Theseus, conflicting accounts of Ariadne), keeping each work and version distinct.

question.prompt: What evidence is needed for the comparison?

choices.text: Only a modern ranking of heroic strength
Both Plutarch’s unification account and the Library’s service account
Only an Iliad quotation about Achilles

question.explanation: Both Plutarch’s unification account and the Library’s service account is the passage-specific answer. Check Plutarch: Lives of the Noble Grecians and Romans (Life of Theseus, the unification narrative); Bibliotheca (Library) (Library 2.4.12, oracle assigns service), keeping each work and version distinct.
